Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

CycloDesk 0.2.2 (alpha)

  • Menus in the order of the work, with submenus by subject: Basic Series (make or load a series), Processing (was Math; now also detrending and pre-whitening), Time Series (spectra, evolutive spectra, wavelets, significance, filtering, two series, decomposition, nonlinear analysis, noise), Sed. rate (tracking, TimeOpt, COCO, other tests), Age models (building, anchoring, dated levels, uncertainty, checks, correlation) and Astronomy. The separate Wavelets menu is now part of Time Series, and the geological time scale moved from Astronomy to Age models > Anchor to absolute ages. The place of every tool is set in one list (R/menus.R).
  • Five tabs in the order of the work (were eight): Data, Plot, Processing, Analysis & age models, R code & log. Processing holds the tools of the menus Basic Series and Processing and the colour record from an image; Analysis & age models holds the tools of Time Series, Sed. rate, Age models and Astronomy, with Track and Anchor. Track, Anchor and Image are views inside these two tabs (a small row under the tabs), no longer tabs of their own. Each of the two tabs starts with a list of its tools and a search box, and comes back to the view it showed last. The R code and the log are side by side in one tab.
  • The Plot tab shows every kind of file: data series, spectra written by the spectrum tools (power with its confidence levels and labelled peaks, on a log axis) and saved results (.cyclodesk.rds, for example a scalogram). New option “Log value axis”.
  • File panel: drag its edge to make it wider (full file names) or collapse it to a ribbon for a larger work area; the width is remembered. A delete button and a right-click menu (plot, rename, duplicate, delete, open the folder) next to Edit > Delete and the Del key.
  • Languages: the interface (menus, tabs, tool names, settings, help texts, dialogs) is available in English, French, Dutch, German, Spanish and Simplified Chinese. CycloDesk starts in the language of the computer when it has that language; change it under Help > Language. Each language is one text file (inst/i18n/<code>.tsv), so corrections and new languages are easy to add (see inst/i18n/README.md). Figures, result texts, the R code and the log stay English. The choices of radio buttons and tick-box groups are translated as well.
  • Geological time scale (Age models > Anchor to absolute ages): shows the table of the installed WaverideR, which now follows the International Chronostratigraphic Chart 2026/06 (it was the chart of 2016, with some errors). The result files are named GTS_... (were GTS2020_...).
  • PDF, PNG and R files and the working folder open with the system’s program on macOS and Linux as well.

CycloDesk 0.2.1 (alpha)

  • CycloDesk is a desktop program: the installers start it in its own window (a small native program, installer/shell), with its own icon in the taskbar or Dock; closing the window closes CycloDesk. Links to other sites open in the web browser.
  • Windows installer: CycloDesk crashed at start-up on some computers (“Mingw-w64 runtime failure: 32 bit pseudo relocation … out of range”), depending on where Windows placed the packages spam and fields in memory. These are now built from source; the installer test checks every package for this problem.
  • The installed CycloDesk ignores the settings and packages of another R on the same computer.

CycloDesk 0.2.0 (alpha)

  • Installers for Windows, macOS and Linux (installer/, GitHub workflow installers): one file per system (.exe, .pkg for Apple silicon and Intel, .sh) that brings its own R (conda-forge) with all packages, installs without administrator rights and adds a desktop/menu icon. Built and tested on GitHub for every release and attached to it. “Update and restart” now also works in these installed copies on all three systems.
  • Four new menus give access to most of WaverideR (about 50 more tools):
    • Wavelets: adaptive wavelet, superlet and chirplet synchrosqueezing, ConceFT, chirp-matched EHA and wavelet, de-chirped scalograms, wavelet/SST/band significance and surrogates, extraction of signal, power and amplitude (stable band or along a track), dynamic filtering, transients, Bayesian/SWA/MESA spectra, frequency and wavelet uncertainty.
    • Sed. rate: astronomical HMM and iterative tracking, chirp-steered tracking and rate-grams, FLMW, MESA tracking, cross-validated and adaptive (e)COCO with ridge tracking, windowed TimeOpt with several fits, the astronomical sedimentation-rate and tuning tests, legacy PDA.
    • Age models: minimal tuning, conversion with a track, sedimentation rate or anchor points, Monte Carlo re-tracking and age-model uncertainty (floating or anchored), gap durations, modified Bchron and astroMCBchron, age-model check against the de-chirped record, exponential sedimentation ramps.
    • Astronomy: astronomical periods at any age and through time, term identification, bundling ratios, chaotic resonance, CTest and the precession constant, tests of tuned records, the Earth-Moon system, the geological time scale.
    • Math > More (WaverideR): maxima/minima, lag-1 autocorrelation, litholog discretisation, change-point R2, coloured noise.
  • About 50 tools for the astrochron functions that were not yet reachable, and for DecomposeR, lomb and dtw:
    • astrochron: cleaning, tapers, resampling at the levels of a second file, Laepple-Huybers interpolation, peaks, moving-window statistics and correlation, summary statistics, cross-plots, stratPCA, accumulation rates, rank series (Math > More (astrochron)); lowpass/highpass/kernel detrending; synthetic series, insolation series and maps, the Imbrie ice-volume model, sedimentation-rate ramps and differential accumulation, synthetic stratigraphy, bioturbation (Basic Series); spectral peak tests with multiple-testing corrections, testBackground, EHA band power, WOSA bicoherence, surrogates, surrogateCor/slideCor, the bioturbation impulse response (Time Series); TimeOpt with Monte Carlo significance, timeOptTemplate, Bayesian TimeOpt and MCMC, eTimeOptTrack, ASM/eASM, testPrecession/testTilt, freq2sedrate (Sed. rate); anchorTime, wtMean/stepHeat (Age models); bergerPeriods/calcPeriods, hoangPriors, alodfromk, tones (Astronomy).
    • DecomposeR (Time Series > Empirical mode decomposition): EMD and ensemble EMD, singular spectrum analysis, instantaneous frequency and amplitude of the modes, ratios between modes, precision of the Hilbert frequency.
    • Other packages: Lomb-Scargle periodogram for uneven sampling (lomb), Fourier cross-spectral coherence and phase, recurrence plots, correlation of two records by dynamic time warping (dtw, Age models).
    • DecomposeR, lomb and dtw are suggested packages: the launcher installs them, and a tool that needs a missing one says how to install it.
  • Menus keep the tools of one group together, with the astrochron and other-package groups next to the CycloDesk group of the same name.
  • Track > Helper lines: groups of lines are added and removed in a list, each with its own colour, line type and label. Line types: periods of cycles (kyr) scaled by the current track or by an age-model file; fixed periods in depth units; or any column of a file against a depth column, times a multiplier (e.g. 4.05 turns a sedimentation rate in cm/kyr into the 405-kyr period in m). Boundary lines can be read from a column of a file and cleared with one button; typed or clicked boundaries keep 6 significant digits (were 3, which rounded depths above 999). After Add, and below the scalogram, CycloDesk says how many helper lines there are and which lie outside the period range shown (for example an age column picked as a period). On a sedimentation-rate map (eCOCO, eTimeOpt) fixed values and file columns are drawn as rates (cm/kyr).
  • Image tab (File > Colour record from an image): click a route on an outcrop photograph, core scan, tree-ring image or satellite image, set the scale with a scale bar, and get grey value, L*a*b*, RGB and HSV averaged over a swath along the route (cd_image_profile()).
  • Track tab works on every map: wavelet, superlet and synchrosqueezed scalograms, EHA, windowed FFT, EHA on a log2 axis and evolutive MESA (period tracks), and eTimeOpt, win_timeOpt and eCOCO (sedimentation-rate tracks, converted directly to an age model). “Track on this map” in the Tool tab opens any of them.
  • Zoom in the Tool tab: drag a box on the figure or type the x and y limits; double-click resets. Spectra label the peaks inside the zoomed range, so a peak can be read off and used for a filter band.
  • Padding of sliding-window analyses (EHA, eTimeOpt, eCOCO): mirror or mean padding by half a window, so the result spans the whole record (cd_pad_ends()).
  • Citation: “Arts, M. (2026). CycloDesk: Graphical Interface for Cyclostratigraphy. R package version 0.2.0. https://github.com/stratigraphy/CycloDesk”.
  • Fixes: evolutive figures failed with “figure margins too large” in narrow windows; a clearer message when eTimeOpt cannot test the chosen rates; long menus scroll.

CycloDesk 0.1.0 (alpha)

First public release, for testing and feedback. Menus, defaults and file names may still change.

  • Working-folder workflow: file browser with drives, places, filter, drag-and-drop (Ctrl = copy); text, csv (also with semicolons and decimal commas), Excel and LAS files.
  • Plot, Basic Series, Math and Time Series menus with about 40 tools, all calling WaverideR or astrochron; every result is written next to its input with an Acycle-style suffix, and the R code of each step is collected in the R code tab.
  • Spectral analysis (MTM, LOWSPEC, MESA, AMTM, SWA, …), evolutive spectra, wavelets (22 mother wavelets), superlets and synchrosqueezing with 17 colour palettes, coherence, cross wavelet and bispectral analysis.
  • Track tab: track a cycle by hand on the scalogram (snap to peaks, free points, HMM ridge following, snapping the whole curve to the nearest peaks, LOWESS smoothing), helper lines for other cycles, boundary lines, floating age model, extraction of any cycle, and a tuning check with the amplitude modulation.
  • Anchor tab: tie a floating record to La2004/La2010/La2011, insolation or a metronome by clicking matching peaks.
  • Filtering, age models, tuning, TimeOpt/eTimeOpt, COCO/eCOCO, rho1, DYNOT, PDA and spectral moments.
  • Windows launcher (SETUP.bat) with a desktop shortcut; checks once a day for new versions of CycloDesk and WaverideR on GitHub.
